active.title: Spark pk/fk parity — SparkGenerator generates the same keys as DataGenerator, bit for bit
active.description: In 0.7.0 SparkGenerator rejects pk/fk ('NumPy engine only in 0.7.0'). Design: port the key function to native Spark expressions over spark.range(size) — F.xxhash64(F.lit(col_seed).cast('long'), F.col('id')) matches the NumPy xxh64_long bit for bit (prototype spark_parity.py, 50k rows); F.pmod for the parent index; sequence and affine permutation are plain arithmetic; Feistel as a native round loop or mapInPandas over the NumPy core. No Python UDF; never F.rand(seed), whose output changes with the partition count. Parity test: same spec and seed on both engines give identical pk/fk columns. The NumPy core stays the reference; a pure addition, since 0.7.0 keys are hash- and index-based.
active.provenance: operator grill 2026-10-03 (main thread, release 0.7.0 rc-1) D3: "Out; backlog it (Recommended)"

active.title: DB key-sink writer — write generated frames or keys to a database, output only, never a lookup
active.description: 0.7.0 deletes the SQLite/DuckDB checkpoint. Design: an optional writer beside the file writers (.write.format('sqlite'|'duckdb') or a sink callable) persisting generated frames or key columns to a database for users who want their tables there. Output only: no generator ever reads keys back; keys stay a pure function of the definition, the seed and the row index. The DB driver is an optional extra, never a core dependency (constitution invariant 10); table and column identifiers are validated or quoted (invariant 8); needs its own approved SPEC and security review (constitution Exclusions). Tests read rows back from a database under pytest tmp_path.
active.provenance: operator grill 2026-10-03 (main thread, release 0.7.0 rc-1) D2: "Delete + backlog a key sink (Recommended)"

active.title: Event-time-ordered FK (born_before) — a child references only parents born at or before its event time
active.description: The old watermark's intent, rebuilt statelessly (load-realism phase). Design: event time is a function of the row index (born(i) = start + i/rate) for parent and child; an fk kwarg born_before limits the child's parent index range to parents born at or before the child's event time — alive(j) = number of parent indices with born(p) <= t(j), p = sampler(hash(seed, j)) mod alive(j), skew applied over permuted ranks as in 0.7.0. No clock, no database; parent and child producers need no coordination across processes. Market study prototype: no child before its parent, identical output for 1 or N chunks.
active.provenance: operator grill 2026-10-03 (main thread, release 0.7.0 rc-1), SPEC 0.7.0 rc-1 open question 5: "Backlog it (Recommended)"

active.title: stream_dict via Arrow — build streamed records through pyarrow instead of df.to_dict('records')
active.description: Deferred from 0.7.0 rc-1 (SPEC out-of-scope line: "stream_dict via Arrow → backlog (break needs its own ruling)"). Design: build each microbatch's records with pyarrow.Table.from_pandas(df, preserve_index=False).to_pylist() instead of df.to_dict('records'); a probe measured about 4x faster. Same native types, but two breaks: a mixed-type transformer output column raises ArrowInvalid, and NaN becomes None. Before it enters a candidate it needs (1) an operator ruling on that break and (2) its FR11 stream_dict sink row measured before and after. pyarrow is already a runtime dependency; nothing is added.

active.title: PyPI metadata — wider keywords, Typing :: Typed, advertised Python versions equal the tested 3.10–3.13
active.description: Release 0.8.0, candidate rc-2: drafted in a define tree while rc-1 implements, it enters at rc-1's CLOSURE; a candidate is never amended, a new AC goes to the next rc (specs/releases/AGENTS.md:26-27). Demand: PyPI search discoverability, and advertised Python versions equal to the tested ones. Measured baseline (poetry build --format wheel on 7e12958): the wheel METADATA has 6 keywords (pyproject.toml:11), no Typing :: Typed, and Classifier Programming Language :: Python :: 3 plus 3.10 through 3.15, which poetry-core derives from python = "^3.10" (pyproject.toml:26); the CI test matrices run only 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 (.github/workflows/auto_tag_publish_master.yml:74, auto_tag_publish_development.yml:83, test_on_push.yml:40, pr_to_master.yml:31, pr_to_development.yml:158). Outcome: (1) keywords keep the existing 6 and add faker, fake-data, pyspark, spark, pandas, kafka, parquet, data-generator; (2) classifier Typing :: Typed (the py.typed marker lands in rc-1 AC3.2); (3) every CI test matrix gains Python 3.13, Spark tests skip where pyspark 3.5 cannot run, so CI tests 3.10-3.13; pyproject keeps python = ">=3.10" with no upper cap (installable on 3.14+), and states the classifiers Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 explicitly, so the wheel advertises only the tested set. The rc-2 as-is review confirms poetry-core keeps the hand-written classifiers and adds no 3.14+ classifier from the range; if it cannot, the fallback is python = ">=3.10,<3.14". Asserted on the wheel's METADATA: the 14 keywords, Typing :: Typed, and no Programming Language :: Python :: 3.x classifier beyond 3.10-3.13; each assert is RED on today's wheel. The rc-2 PLAN names the wheel test that owns these asserts; the existing one is test_wheel_exposes_faker_only_as_the_approved_optional_extra (tests/integrations/test_public_api.py:392), and all share one wheel build.
